text:
anya: quick flag from v3-small PTQ bringup: overall NDCG@10 ~unchanged but short-query MRR@5 down ~4.2%. No tokenization diffs.

dmitri: that smells like top-k reordering / score compression from quant. did we keep candidate slots stable?

anya: eval harness had shuffle enabled by mistake and we use numpy.argsort for metric order. might be non-deterministic for ties.

carmen: numpy.argsort instability + PTQ compressing tiny score gaps is a bad combo. can you run controlled seeds w/ no-shuffle and stable tiebreaker?

anya: ran 3 quick reproductions (seeded):
- no-shuffle + stable id tiebreak, top-10 -> MRR@5 -0.8%
- no-shuffle + stable id tiebreak, top-3 -> MRR@3 -4.0%
- control (shuffle) top-3 -> MRR@3 -4.4%
NDCG@10 unchanged. gap concentrated in top-3.

kevin: do score-delta histograms between FP32 and PTQ for top-5. if many deltas are ~0 then ties explain MRR drop.

anya: summary hist: exact-equal top-3: FP32 0.09%, PTQ 1.6%. delta <1e-4: FP32 1.1%, PTQ 5.9%.

tess: good data. two mitigations: (1) stable tie-breaker by candidate_id in eval + prod, (2) keep final logits in fp16 or apply tiny deterministic offset. prefer (1) then (2).

anya: implemented tie-breaker shim and re-ran: MRR@3 gap -> ~0.9%. with last-layer fp16 + tie-breaker -> ~0.4%.

dmitri: add offline metric "topk_exact_ties" and a rankbench smoke that asserts PTQ MRR drop <1% on short-query cohort.

anya: will open PR with artifacts, histograms, and tests. creating issue INF-800 assigned to me for followups.

ci-bot: run: build-882 uploaded artifacts -> https://ci.redwood/job/882/artifacts

carmen: thanks team 0 — much better than reverting PTQ.
